To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the school environment can be modified to improve children's eating and physical activity behaviors.
the school food environment and physical education (PE) are important factors that can influence children’s eating and physical activity behaviours.

1) the prevalence of obesity among U.S. children and adolescents has increased dramatically over the past 30 years, 2) obesity has become a serious public health problem in the United States and around the world, 3) the prevalence of overweight and obesity is increasing among adults as well as among children and adolescents, 4) overweight and obesity are associated with serious health problems, 5) the causes of obesity are complex and multifaceted, 6) obesity can be prevented
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the ways in which school food environments and policies influence the food choices and eating behaviours of students.
the social and environmental determinants of childhood obesity, particularly the influence of school environments on the health of children.
the development and evaluation of interventions designed to promote healthy eating in schools.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence for a link between the school environment and children’s weight is weak.
the current evidence base supports the implementation of school-based health promotion interventions to prevent obesity in children and adolescents.

the evidence for the effectiveness of school based obesity prevention programmes is limited and that the evidence for school based interventions to promote healthy eating, physical activity and/or body weight is mixed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the schools can be a powerful setting for obesity prevention and that there are a variety of school-based interventions and policies that have the potential to improve children's diets and physical activity.
the schools are a critical setting for promoting physical activity and nutrition, particularly for children.
the obesity epidemic is a public health problem that requires a comprehensive approach to prevention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to do more to help children eat better, and we need to do it now, because the consequences for their future are so dire.
schools have a unique opportunity to influence children's eating and physical activity behaviours, and that this influence extends beyond the school gates.
the school is a powerful place for obesity prevention and that schools can play a major role in promoting healthy eating and physical activities.
